text:
ingrid: FYI raised by a customer — they see a bunch of weird embedding cache behavior after a model upgrade. reported: unexpected cache misses on identical inputs, then a few exact-match hits later. also seeing some dim mismatch errors in their ingest pipeline. attaching notes below. :thinking:
ingrid: Customer says they're using a per-tenant prefix (tenant_id) when calling the embeddings endpoint, but sometimes results look like coming from another tenant's cache. they're worried about leakage/billing. ticket #INC-9871 created.
ingrid: Repro snippet they gave (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["hello world"],"cache_prefix":"acct-42"}'
```

marta: grabbing logs for the period. can you paste the exact request ids from the customer?
ingrid: They gave two request ids: rreq_01F8...A and rreq_01F8...B. timestamps 2025-11-03T14:05:12Z and 14:07:33Z.

sre-bot: Log search results: found matching requests on node g2-serv-03. Both requests routed to the same cache shard (shard-7). cache hit ratio shows miss then hit within ~2m window.

devon: quick hypothesis: prefix normalization bug + batch dimension mismatch. we've seen a case where empty-string prefixes get collapsed and reuse the last non-empty prefix in memory when multiple goroutines mutate the cache key buffer. Could explain cross-tenant hits.

sam: also saw a recent change where we stopped including embedding dimension in the cache key for "auto-detect" model aliases. if the model alias maps to different dimension variants (e.g., open-embed-1536 vs open-embed-384) that would cause silent mismatches when clients batch heterogeneous inputs. but that should produce a dim-check failure, not cross-tenant leakage.

marta: customer saw a 400 with message "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 384" for a batch request right after the first miss. they said they batch mixed-length texts and multiple models from a wrapper service.

ingrid: customer claim: they only call one model (open-embed-1536) from their app, but we shouldn't trust that at face value — they have a sidecar that may call a fallback model on errors.

devon: can we reproduce locally? steps: spin up a small script that sends: 1) single embedding call with prefix "acct-42" 2) immediately another with same text but through a different worker that intentionally omits the prefix or sets it to empty string, 3) then a batch that includes one short vector using alias that resolves to 384. see if shard returns hit for the first text.

ingrid: customer provided a repro-ish trace:
```
14:05:12 req rreq_01F8...A POST /embeddings body:{model:open-embed-1536, prefix:acct-42, input:["hello world"]}
14:05:12 cache key computed: shard7:acct-42:open-embed-1536:hash(hello world) -> MISS
14:05:12 stored vector dim=1536
14:07:33 req rreq_01F8...B POST /embeddings body:{model:open-embed-1536, prefix:"", input:["hello world"]}
14:07:33 cache key computed: shard7::open-embed-1536:hash(hello world) -> ???
14:07:33 returned HIT and payload vector dim=1536
14:08:01 req rreq_01F8...C POST /embeddings body:{model:open-embed-384, prefix:acct-42, input:["tiny"]}
14:08:01 error: dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 384
```

sam: that trace is useful. the weird part is the second request had prefix empty but got a HIT — should have been a different key. devon mentioned a buffer reuse bug in cache key builder. iirc we do: `buf.Reset(); buf.Write(prefix); buf.Write(':'); buf.Write(modelKey)` etc. if a goroutine races and reuses buf without zeroing prefix when prefix=="" we may end up with previous "acct-42" present in the buffer.

marta: good catch. we shipped a small optimization last month to reuse key buffers from a sync.Pool and removed a defensive `WriteString` guard. that could cause exactly this.

devon: quick mitigation: add an explicit `buf.WriteByte(0)` or pre-allocate and copy prefix into a new slice for now. i'll push a hotfix to the cache library and roll to shard-7 first.

ops-bot: Deploy planned: cache-key-fix v2025.11.3 -> rolling to shard-7 (canary 10% traffic) in 10m.

ingrid: customer also mentioned unexpected billing spike: they were charged for the 3rd request that errored with dim mismatch. can we confirm billing behavior? billing team: are error requests billable?

sam: by policy, we bill successful model calls; if we returned 400 before calling the model, it should not be billed. but if the request hit the model and model returned vectors before we rejected for cache dim check, it might be billable. need to check pipeline ordering.

marta: looking at pipeline: we currently do cache lookup -> if miss then call model -> on model response we validate dims -> attempt to insert into cache -> return response. That means if model returns but validation fails, model call still happened (billable). for some clients that triggered our fallback logic (their wrapper retried different model) causing multiple billable calls.

ingrid: action items for support: 1) notify customer we've identified probable cache key race causing prefix reuse and a hotfix is rolling to canary. 2) suggest they avoid aliasing models in the same batch until we confirm. 3) offer to reverse charges for the apparent erroneous calls while we audit.

devon: engineering action items: 1) push cache-key-fix hotfix and monitor canary (ops-bot reported canary in 10m). 2) add dimension to cache key for any aliasing models and add a server-side check to reject mixed-dim batches with a clear 400 and no model invocation. 3) add unit test that runs concurrent key builds with empty prefix to reproduce race.

marta: i'll own the rollback/monitoring plan. will attach Sentry and metric alerts: cache_hit_rate, cross_tenant_hit_count (new), model_call_count_per_request.

ops-bot: Canary deployed to shard-7 (10% traffic). health: OK.

ingrid: I've emailed the customer with interim note: we rolled a canary fix for cache key normalization and are auditing billed calls. asked for any additional repro logs. they asked for ETA on full roll — said asap after canary looks good.

sam: note for postmortem: consider making prefix a required non-empty field for tenant-scoped caches (server-side validation). also review `sync.Pool` reuse of buffers in hot paths for safety.

devon: patch PR: https://internal.redwood/repo/cache/PR-614 (internal link). contains both zeroing and adding dim into key. requesting review from sam/marta.

marta: pct canary look good for 20m, increasing to 50%. no further cross-tenant hits seen on shard-7 logs.

ingrid: customer replied: "thanks, we appreciate quick response — let's keep me posted and please reverse any charges that look wrong." :thumbsup:

marta: will run billing audit for tenant acct-42 and propose refund for 3 suspicious calls.

devon: after full rollout, follow up with unit tests + chaos-run to stress concurrent key builds.

ingrid: closing loop: will update ticket INC-9871 and schedule a short postmortem doc.

sre-bot: Postmortem draft created: /internal/pmems/INC-9871-cache-prefix-race.md

ingrid: thanks everyone. keep thread updated if you see other tenants with similar patterns. :eyes:
